title: A study to find out if early microsurgery to repair damaged lymph vessels can reduce arm swelling after lymph node removal surgery for cancer treatment
official: A feasibility multicentre randomised controlled trial on microsurgical immediate lymphatic reconstruction to reduce risk of lymphoedema
summary:
Background and study aims 
Surgery for cancer sometimes requires removal of the lymph nodes in the armpit, known as axillary lymph node clearance (ALNC). While this is often necessary for cancer treatment, it carries a risk of causing lymphoedema, a long-term condition that results in painful and disabling swelling of the arm. Lymphoedema can have a major impact on quality of life and currently there are no proven ways of preventing it.
This study is testing whether it is possible to introduce a new surgical technique, called immediate lymphatic reconstruction (ILR), alongside standard cancer surgery. ILR involves reconnecting small lymphatic vessels to tiny veins in the armpit during the operation. This is done using microsurgery and adds around 60 minutes to the procedure. The aim is to restore lymphatic drainage and reduce the risk of developing lymphoedema in the future.

Who can participate? 
Patients aged 18 years and over with breast cancer or skin cancer of the trunk who need ALNC

What does the study involve? 
Participants will be randomly allocated by computer to one of two groups. One group will receive standard surgery (ALNC alone), while the other group will receive ALNC with ILR. All patients will be followed for up to 2 years. At each follow-up, doctors and nurses will assess the arms for swelling, carry out simple tests such as arm measurements and bioimpedance (a painless electrical measurement), and ask participants to complete questionnaires about wellbeing and quality of life. In some centres, an additional test called indocyanine green (ICG) lymphography may also be used.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
The main purpose of this feasibility study is to test whether this type of trial is practical and to gather early safety data. If successful, the results will inform the design of a larger trial to properly test whether ILR prevents lymphoedema.

Where is the study run from? 
The Royal Free Hospital (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
October 2026 to September 2029

Who is funding the study? 
The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults ≥18 years old
2. Diagnosis of breast cancer or skin cancer of the trunk requiring ALNC (with or without neoadjuvant or adjuvant systemic treatment)
3. Patient understands and is willing to consent, can comply with follow-up regime and able to respond to the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
1. Skin cancer of the ipsilateral upper limb requiring surgical excision
2. Fungating axillary lymph node disease requiring soft tissue reconstruction 
3. Inflammatory breast cancer
4. Previous history of upper limb cancer or lymphoedema
5. Prior ipsilateral axillary radiation
6. High risk for general anaesthesia (GA) or not fit for surgery (ASA classification >4)
